newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet sees losses continuing in Q1.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet sees losses continuing in Q1.

text.p: ValuJet Inc, reporting a $20.6 million loss for the 1996 fourth quarter, said Wednesday that losses would continue in the 1997 first quarter and possibly in the second quarter,
In a conference call, ValuJet spokeswoman Marcia Scott ascribed the anticipated loss in part to nonrecurring costs for preparing 30 aircraft for service later this year.

"These expenses, combined with our limited number of revenue-generating aircraft in service, and competitive pressure on our fares, will result in a loss for the first quarter and possibly for the second quarter," Scott said.
"We do not expect our cost per ASM (available seat mile) to return to the level attained at year-end 1995 until -- at the earliest -- the third of fourth quarter of this year," she said.
The discount carrier today reported a loss of $0.38 per share for the 1996 fourth quarter. The consensus of analsts' estimates was a loss of $0.30, according to First Call.

Twenty-two planes in a ValuJet fleet of 43 DC-9s are operational. Scott said the carrier hoped to have 30 aircraft in service by the end of summer. Thirteen are on offer for sale or lease and two are already the subject of negotiations.

A fleet of 30 aircraft is widely seen on Wall Street as the point at which ValuJet's operations would start to make a profit. Analysts initially had expected 30 planes to be flying by the end of March.
ValuJet President Lewis Jordan later said the airline had not given up on long-term plans to grow beyond the 30-plane mark. "There is no intent there to imply that we would stop at 30," he said.
ValuJet said it was in talks on loan covenants with seven lenders and hoped to get an agreement soon. It already has a preliminary agreement with some lenders.
